report.summary: Chunk 7 of 7: transcript tail anchor, read_anchor, and verify_chain function with tamper verification logic.
risks: verify_chain | medium | The function reads the entire transcript into memory; large files could cause memory issues. | Determine if file size is bounded or implement streaming.

verify_chain | low | If a line fails JSON parsing, prev_entry_sha is not updated, potentially causing false linkage failures for subsequent lines. | Evaluate if this behavior is intended; if not, consider updating prev_entry_sha from the record if possible.

handoff.purpose: Provides functions for loading transcripts, reading anchors, and verifying chain integrity.

symbols.name: load_transcript
symbols.note: Loads transcript from file; returns list of dicts, one per JSON line.

symbols.name: read_anchor
symbols.note: Reads anchor file and returns dict; returns None if missing or invalid JSON.

symbols.name: verify_chain
symbols.note: Verifies chain integrity: checks body_sha, entry_sha, prev linkage, and optional anchor-based count/head checks.

claims.text: ``(record_count, head_entry_sha)`` -- the tail anchor, recomputed from the file. Compare against :func:`read_anchor` to catch a truncation.

Three independent checks per line: * ``body_sha`` recomputed over the canonical body -- catches a content edit; * ``entry_sha`` recomputed over ``(prev, stored body_sha, ts)`` -- catches a back-dated ts or a rewritten link where body_sha WAS updated; * ``prev`` equals the previous line's ``entry_sha`` -- catches a deleted or reordered line (the survivor points at a vanished predecessor).
claims.why: The code performs these three checks: body_sha mismatch, entry_sha mismatch (via _entry_sha(prev, stored_body, ts)), and prev linkage check against prev_entry_sha.

claims.text: TAIL truncation is the one deletion a per-line walk cannot catch (a valid chain's prefix is a valid chain), so the persisted anchor is consulted by default and a shortfall in count or head is NAMED.
claims.why: The code reads anchor via read_anchor and compares expected_count and expected_head against actual count and head, reporting failures.

claims.text: Explicit ``expected_count`` / ``expected_head`` override it; ``use_anchor=False`` verifies linkage only.
claims.why: The code only reads anchor if use_anchor and expected_count/expected_head are None. If use_anchor=False, anchor is not used, and expected_count/expected_head remain None unless provided.

observations.what: load_transcript and transcript_head are defined but not exported in __all__? Not visible in this chunk.
verify_chain references _body_sha and _entry_sha which are not defined in this chunk.
read_anchor returns None on JSONDecodeError, which is consistent with docstring but silently ignores corrupt anchor.
In verify_chain, if a line fails JSON parsing, prev_entry_sha is not updated, which may cause subsequent linkage failures.
The function verify_chain reads the entire file into memory via read_text; large transcripts may cause memory issues.
